DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http:/!pww.dilq.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 89 s. 2021 July 22, 2021 DIRECTOR RUPERTO B. MARIBBAY, JR. Provincial Director, DILG-Cagayan rbmaribay@dilg.gov.ph dilgcagayannorth@yahoo.com Dear PD Maribbay: This has reference to your letter dated 18 March 2021 requesting for legal opinion relative to leave of absence privileges of local officials, which was forvvarded to the Central Office by Regional Director Jonathan Paul M. Leusen, Jr., DILG-Region. As stated in your letter, herein queries arose in connection with the Legal Education and Policy Discussion with DILG (LEAD with DILG) initiative and Project Research and Enhanced Access on Policy Direction (Project READ), aimed at assisting local government operations by gathering various resources such as Legal Opinions and Policy Guidelines of various government agencies. Specifically, the questions raised in your letter are the following, viz: 1. Whether the accrued leave credits of barangay officials may accumulate for more than one (1) year? If the answer is in affirmative, what is the reckoning period for accumulation, will it be the date of start of the present term or the beginning date of govemment service (including previous terms)? 2. Are barangay officials covered by the expanded maternity leave under Republic Act No. 11210? In case the concemed official is a Barangay Treasurer, what are the remedies available for the barangay considering that aside from the Barangay Treasurer and Punong Barangay, no other official is authorized to sign checks and financial documents in the barangay level? 3. For Punong Barangays and Sangguniang Barangay Members, what will be the basis for deduction on the leave credits, will it be the absence during session days or regular working days?

4. What will be the basis for commutation of leave credits, will it be the rate of honorarium even if there are no services rendered? 5. Are barangay officials with approved leave of absence entitled to honorarium even if there are no services rendered? 6. How many days per year may a barangay official, both elected and appointed, apply for leave of absence? And 7. May an arrested barangay official, whose case is pending before the Office of the Prosecutor or the courts, avail his/her accrued leave credits, such as sick leave or vacation leave? If the answer is in affirmative, may he/she apply while in detention and ask someone to deliver the same to the approving authority? In reply thereto, we shall answer the foregoing queries in seriatim. On the first issue, it may be apt to note at the outset that pursuant to Section 81 of Republic Act No. 7160 otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991 (herein after referred to as 'Code'), elective local officials shall be entitled to the same leave privileges as those enjoyed by appointive local officials, including the cumulation and commutation thereof. Article 71 , Rule XIV, of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of the Code enumerates the elective officials of barangays, thus: "ART. 71. Elective Officials.- The elective officials of xxx barangays are the following: Xxx "Barangays (d) Punong barangay (e) Members of the Sangguniang barangay; and (f) Members of the Sangguniang kabataan." Likewise, Article 118, Rule XVII of the aforesaid IRR of the Code, enumerates the appointive officials of barangays, thus: "ART. 118. Appointive Barangay Officials.- (a) The mandatory appointive barangay officials are as follows: (3) Barangay secretary; and (4) Barangay treasurer."

Corollarily, Section 5 of Civil Service Commission (CSC) Memorandum Circular No. 41 series of 1998 provides that "Elective local officials shall be entitled to the same leave privileges as those enjoyed by appointive local officials, including the cumulation and commutation thereof." Coming now to the subject query, attention is respectfully invited to the pertinent provisions of CSC and Department of Budget and Management (DBM) Joint Circular No. 1 series of 2004, thus: "3.0 Cumulation and Commutation 3.2 Leave credits shall be cumulated up to one year only and shall be commuted yearly. (Emphasis supplied) Hence, to answer query no. 1 succinctly, the answer should be in the negative. Anent the second query, we answer in the affirmative. The coverage of Republic Act (RA) No. 11210 otherwise known as the "105-Day Expanded Maternity Leave LaW' includes female workers in public sector, including the Local Government Units (LGUs). Section 4 thereof provides: "Section 4. Maternity Leave for Female Workers in the Public Sector.— Any pregnant female worker in the govemment service, regardless of employment status, in National Govemment Agencies (NGAs), Local Govemment Units (LGUs), Government-Owned or -Controlled Corporations (GOCCs), or State Universities and Colleges (SUCs), shall be granted a maternity leave of one hundred five (105) days with full pay regardless if the delivery was normal or caesarean." (Emphasis supplied) Corollary thereto, Section 1 (h) Rule II of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of the said Act provides: "h. "Female workers in the public sector" refer to women in govemment service who, in accordance with existing laws, rules and regulations, hold public office by virtue of an appointment issued by the proper appointing officer/authority or by way of election in National Govemment Agencies (NGAs), Local Government Units (LGUs), Govemment- Owned or-Controlled Corporations (GOCCs), State Universities and colleges (SUCs), or Local Universities and Colleges (LUCs).

Further, Section 1, Rule Ill thereof provides, thus: "Section 1. Who are Covered.- The 105-Day Expanded Maternity Leave (EMLL) shall cover the following: 1. Female workers in the Public Sector; 2. Female workers in the Private Sector; 3. Female workers in the Informal Economy; 4. Female members who are voluntary contributions to the Social Security System (SSS); and 5. Female national athletes." (Emphasis supplied) Now, to address the concern about barangay treasurer, please be informed that Section 345 of the Code is categorical when it provides that: "Section 345. Officials Authorized to Draw Checks in Settlement of Obligations. - Checks in obligations shall be drawn by the local treasurer and countersigned by the local administrator. In case of temporary absence or incapacity of the foregoing officials, these duties shall devolve upon their immediate assistants." On the third query, attention is invited to pertinent provisions of the above- mentioned CSC-DBM Joint Circular, viz: "3.3 The cumulation of leave credits of the punong barangay and the barangay kagawad shall be based on their actual attendance in regular sessions of the Sangguniang barangay. For this purpose, the minimum number of regular sessions of the Sangguniang barangay shall be two (2) times a month as required under Article 105 of the Rules and Regulations Implementing the Local Govemment Code of 1991 and shall be equal to twenty four (24) sessions in a year. Scheduled sessions in a month other than required two (2) regular sessions shall be treated as special sessions. The dates of the two (2) regular sessions and the special sessions shall be clearly stipulated and fixed in the intemal rules and procedures of the barangay. 3.4 Attendance of the punong barangay and the barangay kagawad in twenty four (24) regular session xxx year shall eam thiåy (30) days leave credits xxx. Attendance in special sessions shall not eam leave credit and shall not be used to offset absences incurred during regular sessions.

Absences during regular sessions in a given year shall be deducted from the annual leave credit/benfits. 3.5 The cumulation and commutation of leave credits of the barangay secretary and barangay treasurer shall be based on forty (40) hours work a week and subject to applicable Civil Service rules and regulations." Accordingly, this level opines that the basis for deduction on the leave credits will be based on the absence of Sangguniang barangay members during sessions. As regards the fourth query, this level is of the view that the basis for commutation of leave credits will be the rate of honorarium. On this, attention is again invited to Item 4.0 of the aforesaid CSC-DBM Joint Circular, thus: "4.0 Computations 4.1 Computation of the money value of leave credits shall be based on the monthly honorarium actually received by the incumbent barangay official for a particular year subject year subject to the limitation on rates of honorarium as provided under Sections 3.1 and 3.2 of LBC No. 63 s. 1996 and pertinent Department of Budget and Management issuances. 4.2 In detemining the leave credit eamed by puning barangay and barangay kagawad for every regular session attended, the thirty (3) days leave credits under Section 3.1 hereof shall be divided by the twenty—four (24) required number of regular sessions in a year as provided under Secion 3.3 hereof. The computations shall be as follows: 30days 1.25 days leave credits eamed per session 24 Sessions 4.3 The money value of the annual leave benefits of barangay officials shall be computed as follows: Annual Leave Leave Credits Benefit (ALB) Eamed (LCE) Monthly Honorarium (MH) x 20,9166672 2 The equivaEnt number of days in a month for computation of the money value of leave benefit based on the total number of working days per year (251) [Section 40 of CSC MC No. 14, s. 1999] divided by the number of months in a year (12).

Illustrative Examples Punong Barangay A Monthty honorarium = Pl ,OOO.OO Total regular sessions attended = 24 Leave credits eamed = 30 ALB = LCE X MH/20.916667 =30.OOX Pl ,000.00/20.916667 ALB = P 1,434.26 Barangay Secretary A Monthly honorarium = P 600.00 Leave credits eamed = 30.00 ALB = LCE X MH/20.916667 = 30.00XP600.OO/20916667 ALB = P 860.56 On the fifth query, we answer in the affirmative. Anent the sixth query, as provided in Item 3.1 of the subject CSC-DBM Joint Circular, Barangay officials shall be entitled to leave credits/benefits equivalent to thirty (30) days for every year of service in the barangay. And finally, as regards the last query, the CSC Resolution No. 94-2795 dated 19 May 1994 finds application. Pertinent portion of which reads, thus: "The records show that, Mr. Vargas was appointed to the position of Utility Worker on January 2, 1989 under a permanent status. From then, Vargas served as such until January 28, 1991 when he was arrested and subsequently detained in jail for drug pushing and possession of illegal drugs. On January 29, 1991, Vargas filed a vacation leave of absence with pay up to March 15, 1991. However, due to the fact that he was detained, he was not able to file the necessary leave of absence up to the time that he was acquitted and subsequently released from jail on October 13, 1992. On October 14, 1992, Vargas reported back to his post. However, the Municipality of Makati did not act on his request to allow him to reassume his former position. When Mr. Vargas was in jail, his services were considered automatically suspended. He could not be expected to file his corresponding application for leave of absence, because whether he likes or not he could not possibly report to work. He is considered on automatic leave of absence for the period of his detention in jail." Further, the CSC in its Resolution No. 991879 dated 23 August 1999 had elucidated that: "It should be pointed out that the service of an employee who is being detained for failure to put up bail or for non-bailable crime, or for some reasons, is automatically suspended from office. xx"

Applying the foregoing in the case is at bar, query no. 7 should be answered in the negative. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours BY HORITY THE SECRETARY: . DINO ART cr tary for Barangay Affairs DIRECTOR JONATHAN PAUL M. LEUSEN Regional DILG-Region II Tuguegarao City, Cagayan
